title: An invoice made after a reversal takes the customer's term at that moment
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop reverses a Net 30 invoice after the customer moved to Net 60, and invoices it again.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has invoice {Invoice-A} for work order {Work-order-1}, dated Oct 5, 2026, created on Net 30 (due Nov 4, 2026). The customer has since been moved to Net 60.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-07 Customer and {Work-order-1} is S2-15443.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On {Work-order-1}'s Finance tab, open the invoice's menu.
  2. Click Reverse.
  3. Confirm Reverse.
  4. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  5. Click Create Invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu shows Reverse.
  • Step 2: the warning opens.
  • Step 3: the invoice is reversed and Create Invoice shows again.
  • Step 4: the due date reads Dec 4, 2026 (Oct 5 + 60 days).
  • Step 5: the new invoice shows Terms Net 60 and due Dec 4, 2026; Nov 4, 2026 does not come back.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-E3: “An invoice created after a reversal takes the customer's term at that moment, as today: a deactivated term the customer still holds, or the new term after a move or edit. The reversed invoice's old due date does not come back.”
